title: Interaction corrections to topological density three-point functions in two-dimensional Fermi liquids: a coadjoint orbit perspective
authors: Akshay Pal, Andrew Lucas, Umang Mehta
abstract: Density three-point correlations are known to probe the topology of the Fermi sea in two-dimensional noninteracting systems. Here, we study how these correlations are modified by interactions using the coadjoint-orbit effective field theory. A key advantage of the coadjoint-orbit formulation is that it provides a systematic way to incorporate generalized Landau interactions in terms of bosonized degrees of freedom, mapping fermionic loop contributions onto simpler tree-level diagrams. We show that, for a general isotropic dispersion $ε(p)$, even at linear order in the generalized Landau interaction, $\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{F}^{(2,0)})$, there exists a contribution proportional to the band curvature $ε''(p_F)$ that changes the nonanalytic structure of the free density three-point correlation function.   This contribution introduces a distinct nonanalytic structure beyond that found in either the noninteracting case or an interacting Galilean-invariant system, showing that interaction effects can modify the topology-detecting density three-point correlation.
summary: This theoretical paper examines how interactions modify the topological information contained in density three-point correlations in 2D Fermi liquids. Using the coadjoint-orbit effective field theory, the authors calculate interaction corrections, finding a new nonanalytic structure dependent on the band curvature. This shows that interaction effects can fundamentally alter the way the system's topology is probed by these correlation functions.
main_problem: The study investigates how electron-electron interactions modify the topological information encoded in density three-point correlation functions within two-dimensional Fermi liquids.
main_result: Interaction effects introduce a novel nonanalytic contribution to the density three-point function, proportional to the band curvature $\epsilon''(\mathbf{p}_F)$, demonstrating that topology-detecting correlations are sensitive to interaction details beyond simple renormalization.
method: The authors employ the coadjoint-orbit effective field theory to systematically calculate perturbative corrections to the density correlation function, analyzing specific momentum limits to pinpoint nonanalytic behavior.
model_or_system: The system is a two-dimensional Fermi liquid. The analysis compares the behavior of density correlations in the noninteracting limit, the Luttinger liquid (1D), and the interacting 2D case, using the coadjoint-orbit formalism for the latter.
key_observables: The equal-time density three-point correlation function, $\langle\deltaho_{\mathbf{k}} \deltaho_{\mathbf{k}_1} \deltaho_{\mathbf{k}_2}angle$, and its nonanalytic structure near specific momentum configurations.
important_parameters: The band curvature $\epsilon''(\mathbf{p}_F)$ and the generalized Landau interaction parameters $F^{(2,0)}$.
main_assumptions: The calculations rely on the coadjoint-orbit effective field theory framework and assume angle-independent Landau parameters for explicit limit calculations.
figures_summary: The notes reference a figure showing numerical confirmation of a distinct linear cusp in the correlation function near the antiparallel momentum configuration ($\Delta\varphi 	o \pi$).
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first establishing the noninteracting baseline, then applying the coadjoint-orbit formalism to calculate interaction corrections to the three-point function, analyzing the resulting nonanalytic behavior in specific momentum limits.
why_interesting: While focused on Fermi liquids, the use of advanced effective field theories (coadjoint orbits) to probe subtle nonanalytic behavior in correlation functions is a powerful theoretical tool applicable to understanding quantum critical points and interacting many-body systems in general.
